input.command:
mkdir -p out && cat > out/CONVENTIONS_manifold_c.md <<'EOF'
# On-box conventions and the provenance writer (experiment directory `manifold_c`)

This file is the second binding input to the build stage. The design record is
the specification of WHAT to measure. This file is the specification of HOW the
two built files must sit inside the frozen infrastructure that will run them.
Nothing here may be "improved". Where this file and the design record disagree
about a number, the design record wins; where they disagree about a path, a
marker, or a file layout, this file wins.

## 1. The two files you write

    run_<TAG>.py      the measurement, stages `extract`, `calibrate`, `endpoints`
    onbox_<TAG>.sh    the on-box driver that runs those stages in order

`<TAG>` is given to you in the build call. Write these two files in the
experiment directory (the current working directory) and edit nothing that
already exists. In particular `pipeline.js`, `triage_workflow.js`, `gates/`,
`frozen/` and `.claude/agents/` are frozen and read-only.

## 2. The frozen infrastructure you are running inside

Three frozen files, in `frozen/`, are shipped to the rented box unchanged:

  * `frozen/provenance.py`   the record writer (section 4)
  * `frozen/remote_run.sh`   the box bootstrap. It does `cd ~/mats_manifold`,
    installs `pillow jinja2 numpy==1.26.4 scikit-learn transformers accelerate`
    on top of the image's preinstalled CUDA torch, asserts
    `torch.cuda.is_available()` and exits 3 if it is False, then execs the
    command it was handed. It creates no virtual environment. Do not create one
    either, and do not install or pin torch.
  * `frozen/lambda_run.sh`   the local launcher. A per-launch copy of it, with
    only its declared adaptation points changed, does: launch -> poll -> scp the
    payload -> run `bash remote_run.sh bash onbox_<TAG>.sh` detached under
    `setsid` and `timeout` -> poll for a marker -> fetch -> terminate.

Consequences you must respect, because the launcher is frozen:

  * The on-box working directory is `~/mats_manifold`. Your shell script must
    `cd ~/mats_manifold` and must halt loudly if it is missing.
  * The launcher writes `~/mats_manifold/RUN_DONE` itself, from your script's
    exit code, and polls for that file. Your script must NEVER create or remove
    `RUN_DONE` in that directory. Use a differently named marker of your own.
  * The launcher fetches, in this order: `~/mats_manifold/out/*summary*.json`,
    then `~/mats_manifold/out/*.log`, then the whole of `~/mats_manifold/out/`.
    Anything not under `~/mats_manifold/out/` is never fetched and is lost when
    the box is torn down.
  * The launcher tails `~/mats_manifold/out/run_detached.log` for progress, so
    print short one-line progress messages and flush them.
  * The run is capped by `timeout $REMOTE_TIMEOUT` (default 5400 seconds) and
    the box self-destructs at cap plus grace. Design for well under one hour.

## 3. Where results go

Write records under `results_<TAG>/out/` and large intermediates under
`results_<TAG>/work/`. Then copy every fetchable artifact into
`~/mats_manifold/out/`, because that is the only directory the launcher takes.
`work/` is deliberately not copied: it is gigabytes of intermediate arrays that
no record depends on after the run.

Give the single decision-bearing roll-up record a filename containing the word
`summary`, so the launcher fetches it first over a flaky link. The provenance
writer already emits a `<name>_summary.json` beside every record; that is what
satisfies this.

The local result directory is passed to the launcher as its fourth argument and
will be `out/results_<TAG>`; the fetch lands the box's `out/` inside it, giving
`out/results_<TAG>/out/...` locally. Do not hardcode any local path in the
runner.

## 4. The provenance writer: one home per fact

`frozen/provenance.py` is imported as `import provenance` (the launcher ships it
flat into `~/mats_manifold/`). Use exactly these entry points:

    provenance.describe_input(path, n_items=<int>) -> dict
    provenance.write_result(out_path, *, cell, inputs, metric, values,
                            threshold=None, decision_rule="", decision="",
                            notes="", rows=None) -> Path
    provenance.cell_slug(cell) -> str

Rules the writer enforces, and which you must therefore satisfy:

  * `cell` must be flat and JSON-scalar valued. It is the identity of the run.
    The convention in this project's prior seeds is
    `{"arm": ..., "model": ..., "revision": ..., "stage": ...}`, plus
    `"aperture": <int>` on any record that belongs to one probe width.
  * `decision_rule` is REQUIRED and is an argument written before the values are
    known. It states the neutral threshold in terms of the measurement only.
  * The filename must be `cell_slug(cell) + ".json"`, so the path and the
    contents cannot silently disagree.
  * `inputs` must list every file the result was computed from, each through
    `describe_input`, with its item count. This includes the stimulus file, the
    committed design record, the committed gate commit, and any intermediate
    array file the stage read.

Run `python3 provenance.py --selftest` on the box before any measurement, and
fail the run if it exits non-zero.

## 5. Stimulus file

`stimulus_linewrap_v2.json`, sha256
`b0aa4255b5038d6fbc2e7314decf1011a5b5a13990098142e16ab44c6bba41dd`. Shape:

    {"meta": {"widths": [20,40,60,80,100,120,140,200,280], "n_docs": 48,
              "train_docs": 36, ...},
     "docs": [{"id": 0, "split": "train"|"test", "chars": 3595,
               "sha256_plain": "...", "wrapped": {"20": "...", ..., "280": "..."}},
              ...]}

Load it exactly. Never regenerate, re-wrap, paraphrase or reconstruct the text.
If the file is absent, or its hash differs, halt with a non-zero exit before any
graphics-card time. The document split is the file's own `split` field; do not
re-derive it.

## 6. Model and checkpoint

`EleutherAI/pythia-410m-deduped` at HuggingFace revision `step143000`, loaded
with `output_hidden_states=True`. The token `HF_TOKEN` is exported into the run
by the launcher. Read the DOWNLOADED config for the layer count and hidden size
and halt if they disagree with the design's stated values: the config is
authoritative, the design's numbers are recalled and are only a cross-check.
Hidden state index 0 is the embedding output, so a model with `n` blocks yields
`n + 1` readouts.

## 7. Halt discipline

  * The stages are dependent, not parallel legs. A failed stage marks every
    stage that depends on it as skipped, records every exit code, and exits
    non-zero.
  * The calibration stage must write its committed record, from training
    documents only, BEFORE the endpoint stage computes any held-out number.

cat > out/GATE_COMMIT_seedC1.md <<'EOF'
# Gate commit, seed C1 (experiment directory `manifold_c`)

Committed by the operating session, 2026-08-26, before any build and before any
rented box is launched. It answers, of record, every item the design pass
queued: five departure questions from the diff phase, one grounding verdict that
did not reproduce, one run-queue item, one author-queue item, and seven
instrument validations. "Accepted as-is" is an answer here and is used where the
design's own choice stands unchanged.

Binding source of the design: `out/seedC1_design_diff_triage.json`.
Budget: approved at 4 USD against a total cap of 15 USD.
Substrate: one Lambda Cloud box, `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4`, `us-west-2`, 1.99 USD per
hour, launched and torn down by a per-launch copy of the frozen launcher, with
teardown confirmed through the cloud API.

---

## A. Diff departure questions

### A1. "Should the number of periods searched at each window depend on the longest line length in training text, or be fixed some other way?"

Answer: it depends on the training label range, as the design says. ACCEPTED AS
IS in principle, with one arithmetic clamp that is required for the quantity to
exist at all, and one extra recorded number.

The design commits, per probe window, a profile length taken from the largest
label value that occurs at that wrap width in training documents. That is kept.
Two things are pinned so the stage is computable and auditable:

* Let `L` be the number of labels in that window's committed label window. The
  off-diagonal profile `m(delta)` is defined for `delta = 1 .. L - 1`. There is
  no `delta = L`: it would average zero label pairs. The committed profile
  length is therefore `min(committed_max_label_span, L - 1)`, and the clamp, if
  it bites, is written into the calibration record.
* For every `delta` the run records how many label pairs were averaged into
  `m(delta)`. The far tail of the profile rests on a handful of pairs, and that
  thinness must be visible in the artifact rather than inferred.

The periods searched are unchanged and are not narrowed: every whole-cycle
period `P = profile_length / k` for integer `k`, keeping `P >= 4` and
`P <= profile_length`. No search band exists.

Why the design's own rule stands rather than a tighter one: the thin tail
inflates the observed maximum power, but it inflates every shuffle draw's
maximum power in the same way, because the null draws are built from per-label
mean vectors over the same positions and the same label counts. The rank test
therefore stays honest; what a thin tail costs is sensitivity, not validity.
Narrowing the search to protect sensitivity would reintroduce exactly the band
censorship this question was written to remove.

### A2. "Should every chance-comparison shuffle start from the same fixed random point, or should several different starting points be checked?"

Answer: ACCEPTED AS IS. One fixed base seed, value 0, with a separate derived
stream per probe window and per labelling, recorded in the calibration record
before any held-out number exists.

Reason: several starting points would produce several rank tests with no
pre-registered rule for combining them, which is a larger threat to this design
than seed sensitivity is. The seed sensitivity that remains is already carried
by the headline rule: the decision is the invariance fork across three windows,
not any one window's pass or fail.

### A3. "Is this list of test strengths (1, 10, 100, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000) fine enough to trust a pass or fail?"

Answer: ACCEPTED AS IS. The question fixes only that the grid must extend beyond
1000, and it does. Two recorded, never gated, additions: whether the winning
strength sits at an interior grid point or at an edge, recorded separately for
the main selection and for the anchor selection; and the full quality surface
over strength and layer, so a later reader can see how flat the ridge is rather
than take the argmax on trust.

### A4. "Is holding out 6 of the 36 training documents, five separate times, the right amount to set the pass-fail range?"

Answer: ACCEPTED AS IS, with the procedure pinned so that the dispersion
measures what the band has to absorb.

Each of the five resplits runs the WHOLE anchor procedure on its own split, not
just the final fit: it selects the anchor layer on its own sub-training
documents at width 140 alone, fits the ridge on those same sub-training
documents, and scores held-out fit quality on its own six held-out documents at
width 140 alone. The dispersion therefore includes the noise of the layer
selection, which is part of the anchor's definition.

The spread is the median absolute deviation of those five values about their own
median, unscaled (no 1.4826 factor). The half-width is three times that. A
measured spread of exactly zero halts the run as WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE; it is
never emitted as a zero-width band.

Acknowledged limitation, of record: five values is a coarse dispersion estimate,
and the six-document held-out sets are half the size of the twelve-document test
set the band will judge. That is a stated weakness of this run, and it is
carried into the answer of A6 and B1 below rather than fixed by changing the
question's rule.

### A5. "Is a $4 budget on one rented graphics computer, for about one hour, enough to safely finish all three probe windows?"

Answer: yes, and approved. The same instrument, on the same committed text and
the same checkpoint, measured about 37 seconds for the 432 forward passes and
about two minutes for the whole measurement in a prior run of this project. The
launcher's default hard cap is 5400 seconds with a self-destruct backstop past
it. At 1.99 USD per hour the expected charge is well under one hour of box time.
The total cap for this seed is 15 USD, so one full retry launch is affordable
without a further approval.

### A6. Departure raised by the operating session, not by the diff phase: which fit the anchor statistic uses

The question's definition 8 says "held-out fit at width 140 alone, judged at the
layer the calibration stage selects on train documents at width 140 alone". Two
readings exist. Reading one: the single probe of definition 2, fit on training
documents pooled over all nine wrap widths, scored only on width-140 test
documents. Reading two: a ridge fit on width-140 training documents alone, at a
layer selected on width-140 training documents alone.

Answer: reading two, the design's own reading, stands. It is adopted because
definition 8 states that the selection procedure is part of the anchor's
definition, which makes the anchor a self-contained width-140 procedure rather
than a restriction applied to the pooled probe.

Because the two readings give different numbers, and because the band's centre
came from neither of them, the run must RECORD, never gate, all of these at the
same time, so that a void can be told apart from a construct mismatch:

1. the anchor statistic itself (reading two), with its band and its decision;
2. the same held-out fit under reading one: the pooled nine-width probe at the
   main layer, scored on width-140 test documents alone;
3. held-out fit of the pooled nine-width probe at the main layer, pooled over
   the seven wrap widths 20 through 140 (the construct behind the committed
   value 0.781031 in this project's records);
4. held-out fit of the pooled nine-width probe at the main layer, per wrap
   width, all nine widths;
5. the main layer index and the anchor layer index.

None of these five may enter any decision rule. They exist so the record can be
read.

---

## B. Grounding verdict that did not reproduce

### B1. Verdict "diverges": the anchor band's centre belongs to a different construct from the anchor statistic

The reader's note: the design centres the width-140-only anchor band on 0.781,
while this project's committed measurements of width-140-only fits are 0.700601
and 0.549 (recorded in the seed D2 records) and 0.664024 (recorded in the seed
D2.1 records), and the value 0.781031 belongs to a fit pooled over the seven
widths 20 through 140. The reader predicts the run voids.

Answer, of record: the divergence is REAL, ACKNOWLEDGED, and NOT REPAIRED.

The band's centre is fixed by the question at 0.781 and the operating session
does not move it. Moving a pre-registered band because a prediction says it will
fail is the precise failure this pipeline exists to prevent. The half-width is
measured, not guessed, exactly as the question requires.

Three consequences are committed here instead:

* Every number listed in A6 is recorded, so that an out-of-band anchor can be
  read either as instrument drift or as a construct mismatch between the
  anchor statistic and the number its band is centred on. Neither reading is
  chosen in advance.
* If the anchor lands outside its band, the run's own rule stands: every ripple,
  control and represented-range result is void as an instrument fault, the void
  flag is written into every record produced after the gate, and the void is
  reported as the run's outcome. It is not evidence about the model, and the
  write-up must say so in those words.
* The reader's own prediction, that the run voids, is recorded here before the
  run. If the anchor instead lands inside its band, that prediction was wrong
  and the write-up says so.

A separate note on the reader's second observation, that no output artifacts
exist yet: correct, and expected. This gate is committed before the build, so
the only artifacts at this moment are the committed question, the committed
stimulus file, the design record and this file.

---

## C. Run queue

### C1. "Execute the pre-registered pipeline (layer sweep 0-24, ridge grid {1,10,...,100000}) and report main/anchor layer indices, whether ridge strength lands interior or at grid edge, and the anchor-gate R^2 vs its band."

Answer: this item IS this run, and it is approved to execute. It is not a
separate control. The four things it asks for are required outputs: the main
layer index, the anchor layer index, an interior-or-edge flag for each
selection's winning ridge strength, and the anchor statistic printed beside its
own measured band. All four go into the calibration and anchor records and into
the roll-up.

---

## D. Author queue

### D1. "Report the 5 anchor-resplit R^2 values, their MAD, the resulting band, and the observed width-140 test-set R^2 -- confirm the band width is not so narrow that ordinary train/test sampling variance alone would fail it."

Answer: ACCEPTED, and it becomes a required part of the calibration record
rather than a separately authored control, because everything it asks for is
produced by the calibration stage itself.

The calibration record must carry: the five resplit values in order, the five
document identities held out in each resplit, their median, their median
absolute deviation, the half-width (three times that), and the band's two
endpoints. The endpoints record must carry the observed anchor statistic beside
that band and the pass-or-fail decision.

One flag is added, RECORDED and NEVER GATED: `band_half_width_below_0.02`,
true when the measured half-width is under 0.02. A true value does not change
any decision. It is the marker that says the anchor gate, on this run, was
decided by a dispersion estimate too tight for ordinary sampling variation, and
it must be quoted in the write-up whenever the anchor fails.

---

## E. Instrument validations

Seven endpoint readouts were queued because no version of them carries a
committed validation artifact. One artifact answers all seven, and it is
required by the build brief in any case: the built runner's `--selftest`, which
is standard-library only, runs on the processor before any graphics-card time,
both locally and again on the box, and exits non-zero on any failure. Its
output is saved into the fetched results as the validation artifact.

For each queued instrument the planted ground truth is named here, of record.

### E1. Anchor gate readout
Planted rows with a known fit quality and a known band. Cases: a value inside
the band decides in-band; a value outside decides out-of-band AND marks every
record written afterwards `run_valid=false`, per-window files included; a
planted set of five identical resplit values, whose spread is exactly zero,
halts WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE rather than emitting a zero-width band.

### E2. Maximum ripple power readout
Two planted profiles with known answers. First, a synthetic profile carrying one
injected sine wave of a known whole-cycle period plus a known degree-2 trend:
after detrending, the statistic must return that injected period as the location
of maximum power. Second, a flat profile with no injected period, judged against
planted null draws whose maxima all exceed it: it must NOT clear. This is the
end-to-end validation of detrend, transform, period set and maximum.

### E3. Count of windows clearing their own null
Planted per-window decisions covering counts of 0, 1, 2 and 3, each mapping to
the stated outcome, including the case where 0 defers to the represented-range
check.

### E4. Largest wavelength gap in characters
Planted wavelength sets: one whose pairwise gaps are all at or under 10
characters must read INVARIANT; one with a gap over 10 must not; a set with
fewer than two clearing windows must return the undefined-gap value rather than
a number.

### E5. Largest wavelength-to-window ratio gap
Planted ratio sets: all within 0.1 reads PROPORTIONAL once INVARIANT is ruled
out; a wider spread with wavelength gaps also over 10 characters reads MIXED;
exactly one clearing window reads UNDETERMINED and never MIXED.

### E6. Represented-range readout
Planted bins with known within-bin fit qualities and known 50-draw null
distributions: a bin above its own 95th percentile counts as represented, one
below does not, and the bin spanning label 150 is recorded and excluded from the
decision. The eight bins are fixed at label values 1-35, 36-70, 71-105, 106-140,
141-175, 176-210, 211-245 and 246-280; the straddling bin is 141-175. Labels
above 280, which occur only on line-final newline tokens, fall in no bin and are
recorded as excluded. Within-bin fit quality uses the main probe's predictions
on aperture-280 test positions in that bin, with that bin's own label variance
as the denominator; each null draw permutes those same positions' labels among
themselves and recomputes the same quantity.

### E7. Token-position control readout
Planted pairs of wavelengths with a known characters-per-token rate: a converted
gap over 3 characters credits characters; a gap at or under 3 characters with
both labellings clearing credits token position; disagreement on clearing
credits characters regardless of the gap. The characters-per-token rate is
measured per probe window, on that window's own labelled test positions, and all
three rates are recorded. This resolves, of record, a choice a previous asking
of this question left to whatever the code happened to do.

---

## F. Ordering, pinned because two rules in the question depend on it

The stages run extract, then calibrate, then endpoints, and never in another
order.

The calibration stage reads training documents only. It fixes and writes, in one
committed record: the ridge strength and its interior-or-edge flag, the label
window per probe window, the profile length per probe window with its pair
counts, the shuffle seed streams, the anchor layer, the five resplit values,
their median absolute deviation, and the anchor band. That record is complete
and on disk before the endpoints stage reads its first test-document row.

The endpoints stage is the only stage that reads test documents. It selects the
main layer by held-out fit pooled over all nine wrap widths, computes the anchor
statistic and its gate, then the ripple statistic, the nulls, the token-position
control and the represented-range check, in that order.

A failed stage marks every stage that depends on it as skipped, records every
exit code, and exits non-zero.

content.content:
=== onbox_command ===
Launch, from the experiment directory, with a per-launch copy of the frozen launcher whose remote directory is mats_manifold and whose payload list is the seven files below:

  bash lambda_run_seedC1.sh gpu_1x_a100_sxm4 us-west-2 onbox_seedC1.sh results_seedC1

The launcher runs on the box:  bash remote_run.sh bash onbox_seedC1.sh
and writes ~/mats_manifold/RUN_DONE itself from that script's exit code.

Payload that must land flat in ~/mats_manifold/ (the runner halts if any is missing,
because every record must carry all three committed inputs with their hashes):
  run_seedC1.py
  onbox_seedC1.sh
  frozen/provenance.py
  frozen/remote_run.sh
  stimulus_linewrap_v2.json
  out/seedC1_design_diff_triage.json
  out/GATE_COMMIT_seedC1.md
The last two are also found under out/ on the box if they are shipped that way.

To run one step by hand on the box, in this order only:
  python3 run_seedC1.py --stage extract    --results-dir results_seedC1
  python3 run_seedC1.py --stage calibrate  --results-dir results_seedC1
  python3 run_seedC1.py --stage endpoints  --results-dir results_seedC1
Locally, only:  python3 run_seedC1.py --selftest
=== expected ===
WALL CLOCK, one A100 40 GB box: about 15 to 25 minutes end to end, against the launcher's 5400-second cap. Setup and checkpoint download 1 to 3 minutes. Extract 3 to 6 minutes: the 432 forward passes are the measured 37 seconds, the rest is running-sum arithmetic and about 14 gigabytes written to work/. Calibrate 5 to 10 minutes: about 7000 ridge solves of 1024 by 1024, plus 7.5 gigabytes read back. Endpoints 3 to 6 minutes: a 25-readout sweep, then 1200 shuffle draws and 400 bin draws.

COUNTS. 432 forward passes, 48 documents at nine wrap widths. rows_variants.jsonl: 432 rows, each carrying its text verbatim and that text's own sha256, about 1.7 MB. rows_positions_apertures.jsonl: one row per labelled held-out position at the three probe windows, roughly 31,000 to 33,000 rows, about 6 MB. Six null-spectra files, 200 draws each, one file per probe window per labelling, every draw's full per-period power vector, about 2 MB. Six mean-vector files, one per probe window per labelling, about 3.5 MB. 17 records plus calibration.json, run_state.json, five step logs, two self-test logs, the on-box status file and the marker. About 15 MB fetched in total.

EXPECTED COMMITTED WINDOWS, read from the committed text file: every wrap width has training lines of exactly its own width, so the largest training character label is the width plus one. Character label windows 1 to 141, 1 to 201, 1 to 281; profile lengths 140, 200, 280 after the gate commit's clamp, which bites by one at every window and is recorded; periods searched 35, 50, 70. Held-out counts per label at window 280 ran 12 or more in the prior asking, so every label should carry an average vector.

THREE THINGS THE OPERATING SESSION SHOULD KNOW BEFORE LAUNCH.

1. The build brief's stage name "generate" and its "venv plus installs" both conflict with the two binding files. Gate section F pins extract, calibrate, endpoints; the conventions file forbids a virtual environment and a torch install. I followed the binding files and explained both in the code.

2. The design fixes the profile length but is silent on labels the held-out documents never carry. The profile averages label pairs at each distance, so a missing label costs pairs rather than the measurement, and the missing labels and the pair count per distance are recorded. A distance left with zero pairs halts rather than shortening a committed profile after the fact.

3. That case is likely for the token-position control at the wider windows. Its committed window runs to the largest training token label, near 92 at window 280, which one or two training lines carry and the twelve held-out documents may not. The control is then recorded as not computable, with the reason, and the run continues; the headline fork is unaffected. The design gives no ceiling rule for token labels, so none was invented.

Two smaller choices, both recorded in the records themselves: the 95th percentile of a bin's 50 draws interpolates between neighbouring sorted values, and a tie on power resolves to the longer period. Neither is fixed by the design or the gate commit.

A run whose anchor gate fails still finishes and reports VOID_ANCHOR_FAILED, with run_valid=false in every record written after the gate. That is a recorded outcome, not a step failure, so the script exits 0. A halt, a failed check or a failed step exits non-zero.
=== selftest tail ===
dow
     file and into the roll-up alike, with the reason and the band inside those values.
  E2 a planted 28-character wave on a planted curved trend, recovered end to end through
     the profile, the trend removal, the transform, the period set and the maximum; and a
     flat profile against planted draws that all exceed it, which does not clear.
  E3 counts of 0, 1, 2 and 3 clearing windows, including 0 deferring to the range check.
  E4 wavelength sets at, under and over the 10-character cutoff, and the undefined gap.
  E5 ratios within 0.1 after one shared wavelength is ruled out, a mixed case, and one
     clearing window that reads undetermined and never mixed.
  E6 planted bins above and below their own 95th percentile of 50 draws, the bin from 141
     to 175 recorded and excluded, and labels above 280 falling in no bin.
  E7 a converted gap over 3 characters, a gap of exactly 3 with both clearing, and
     disagreement on clearing crediting characters whatever the gap.
Also covered: the whole held-out readout on a planted held-out set of four documents with
a built-in period of 10 characters and one label no document carries; it recovers the
period, ranks first against its shuffled draws, and reports the label it never saw.

Deliberate-break check: with the clearing rule changed from rank 10 to rank 5 in memory,
the self-test returns 1 and prints "FAIL rank 10 clears". Non-zero exit works.

def resplit_plan(doc_order, seed):
    """The five resplits: which six training documents each one holds out, and its folds.

    Each resplit runs the whole anchor procedure on its own split, so it also needs a
    five-way split of its own 30 sub-training documents. Both come from one stream
    derived from the base seed, and both are written into the calibration record.
    """
    import numpy as np
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    perm = list(rng.permutation(len(doc_order)))
    plans = []
    for r in range(N_RESPLITS):
        held_rows = sorted(int(perm[r * RESPLIT_HELDOUT_DOCS + k]) for k in range(RESPLIT_HELDOUT_DOCS))
        sub_rows = [i for i in range(len(doc_order)) if i not in set(held_rows)]
        order = list(rng.permutation(len(sub_rows)))
        folds = {}
        for rank, pos in enumerate(order):
            folds[int(sub_rows[int(pos)])] = rank % N_FOLDS
        plans.append({"resplit": r,
                      "held_out_rows": held_rows,
                      "held_out_doc_ids": [int(doc_order[i]) for i in held_rows],
                      "sub_train_rows": sub_rows,
                      "sub_train_doc_ids": [int(doc_order[i]) for i in sub_rows],
                      "sub_fold_assignment": {str(int(doc_order[i])): folds[i] for i in sub_rows}})
    return plans


def window_for(train_counts_for_width, kind):
    """The committed label window and profile length for one probe window and labelling."""
    counts = {int(k): int(v) for k, v in train_counts_for_width[kind].items()}
    lo, n_labels, span, gaps = committed_label_window(counts)
    length, clamped = clamp_profile_length(span, n_labels)
    periods = whole_cycle_periods(length)
    return {"label_window_low": lo, "label_window_high": lo + n_labels - 1,
            "n_labels": n_labels,
            "committed_max_label_span": span,
            "committed_profile_length": length,
            "clamped_by_one_pair_rule": clamped,
            "label_values_absent_in_training": gaps,
            "nominal_pair_counts": nominal_pair_counts(n_labels, length),
            "n_periods_searched": len(periods),
            "longest_period": periods[0][1], "shortest_period": periods[-1][1],
            "min_training_positions_over_window":
                int(min(counts.get(v, 0) for v in range(lo, lo + n_labels))),
            "training_positions_at_top_label": int(counts.get(lo + n_labels - 1, 0))}

    tot = load_group_sums(work_dir)
    n_read = tot["gram"].shape[1]
    train_groups = ["train_fold%d" % f for f in range(N_FOLDS)]
    test_groups = ["test_w%d" % w for w in WIDTHS]
    common_inputs = [(work_dir / "group_sums.npz", n_read)]

    # 1. The main layer: best held-out fit, pooled over all nine wrap widths.
    per_layer = []
    for layer in range(n_read):
        fit = sums_for_groups(tot, train_groups, layer)
        ev = sums_for_groups(tot, test_groups, layer)
        w, off = ridge_fit_from_sums(fit[0], fit[1], fit[2], fit[3], fit[5], alpha_main)
        r2, _, _ = r2_from_sums(w, off, ev[0], ev[1], ev[2], ev[3], ev[4], ev[5])
        per_layer.append({"readout": layer, "held_out_quality": round(float(r2), 6)})
    main_layer = int(max(per_layer, key=lambda r: r["held_out_quality"])["readout"])

    anchor_r2, _, _ = r2_from_sums(w_a, off_a, test140[0], test140[1], test140[2],
                                   test140[3], test140[4], test140[5])

        per_width[str(wdt)] = round(float(r2w), 6)

        decision_rule=RULE_RECORDED_ONLY,

        notes=("The anchor statistic fits and scores at width 140 alone, which is the "

def document_slices(docs):
    """One array of row positions per document, so a shuffle stays inside a document."""
    import numpy as np
    out = []
    for d in np.unique(docs):
        out.append(np.nonzero(docs == d)[0])
    return out


def shuffle_slots_within_documents(slots, doc_rows, rng):
    """Permute labels among the positions of each document, leaving its counts intact."""
    out = slots.copy()
    for rows in doc_rows:
        out[rows] = slots[rows][rng.permutation(rows.size)]
    return out


def ambient_dimension(centred, target=VARIANCE_TARGET):
    """How many directions carry the target share of the variance. Recorded, never gated."""
    import numpy as np
    sv = np.linalg.svd(centred, compute_uv=False)
    var = sv ** 2
    total = float(var.sum())
    if total <= 0:
        return None, []
    share = (var / total).tolist()
    cum = 0.0
    dim = len(share)
    for i, s in enumerate(share):
        cum += s
        if cum >= target:
            dim = i + 1
            break
    return dim, share[:10]


def pattern_with_null(x, labels, docs, window_lo, n_labels, profile_length, seed, n_draws=N_DRAWS):
    """The observed statistic, its shuffle comparison, and everything worth saving.

    The label multiset of each document is untouched by a shuffle, so exactly the same
    labels carry an average vector in every draw as in the observed measurement. The
    comparison is therefore between like and like.
    """
    import numpy as np
    slots = slots_array(labels, window_lo, n_labels)
    counts = np.bincount(slots[slots >= 0], minlength=n_labels)
    present_idx = np.nonzero(counts > 0)[0]
    label_values = [int(window_lo + int(i)) for i in present_idx]
    missing = [int(window_lo + i) for i in range(n_labels) if counts[i] == 0]
    pairs = pair_index_lists(label_values, profile_length)
    pair_counts = [len(r) for r, _ in pairs]
    empty = [d + 1 for d, c in enumerate(pair_counts) if c == 0]
    if empty:
        raise Halt("distances %r average zero label pairs, because the held-out documents "
                   "carry no position at labels %r; the committed profile length may not be "
                   "shortened after the fact" % (empty[:5], missing[:10]))
    pair_np = [(np.array(r, dtype=np.int64), np.array(c, dtype=np.int64)) for r, c in pairs]
    periods = whole_cycle_periods(profile_length)
    doc_rows = document_slices(docs)

    def statistic(these_slots):
        means, _ = means_by_label(x, these_slots, n_labels)
        mat = means[present_idx]
        centred = mat - mat.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
        cos = cosine_matrix(centred)
        profile = [float(cos[r, c].mean()) for r, c in pair_np]
        return max_power_statistic(profile, periods), profile, centred, means

    observed, profile, centred, means = statistic(slots)
    dim95, shares = ambient_dimension(centred)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    draws = []
    spectra = []
    for i in range(n_draws):
        shuffled = shuffle_slots_within_documents(slots, doc_rows, rng)
        stat, _, _, _ = statistic(shuffled)
        draws.append(stat["max_power"])
        spectra.append({"draw": i, "max_power": stat["max_power"],
                        "wavelength": stat["wavelength"], "cycles": stat["cycles"],
                        "power_by_cycles": stat["powers"]})
    rank = null_rank(observed["max_power"], draws)
    return {
        "observed": observed, "profile": profile, "pair_counts": pair_counts,
        "periods": periods, "draws": draws, "spectra": spectra, "rank": rank,
        "label_values": label_values, "labels_missing_from_held_out": missing,
        "positions_per_label": [int(c) for c in counts.tolist()],
        "mean_vectors": means, "present_rows": present_idx.tolist(),
        "ambient_dimension_at_95_percent": dim95, "variance_share_first_ten": shares,
        "seed": seed,
    }


def save_pattern_artifacts(out_dir, aperture, labelling, result):
    """The full spectrum of every draw, and the average vectors, both saved for audit."""
    import numpy as np
    spec = Path(out_dir) / ("null_spectra_aperture-%d_labels-%s.jsonl" % (aperture, labelling))

def document_slices(docs):
    """One array of row positions per document, so a shuffle stays inside a document."""
    import numpy as np
    out = []
    for d in np.unique(docs):
        out.append(np.nonzero(docs == d)[0])
    return out


def shuffle_slots_within_documents(slots, doc_rows, rng):
    """Permute labels among the positions of each document, leaving its counts intact."""
    out = slots.copy()
    for rows in doc_rows:
        out[rows] = slots[rows][rng.permutation(rows.size)]
    return out


def ambient_dimension(centred, target=VARIANCE_TARGET):
    """How many directions carry the target share of the variance. Recorded, never gated."""
    import numpy as np
    sv = np.linalg.svd(centred, compute_uv=False)
    var = sv ** 2
    total = float(var.sum())
    if total <= 0:
        return None, []
    share = (var / total).tolist()
    cum = 0.0
    dim = len(share)
    for i, s in enumerate(share):
        cum += s
        if cum >= target:
            dim = i + 1
            break
    return dim, share[:10]

def void_the_run(reason: str, out_dir):
    """Mark this run void. Every record written after this carries the flag."""
    RUN_STATE["run_valid"] = False
    RUN_STATE["void_reason"] = reason
    save_run_state(out_dir)
    print("[void] %s" % reason)


def save_run_state(out_dir):
    with open(Path(out_dir) / "run_state.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump({"run_valid": RUN_STATE["run_valid"],
                   "void_reason": RUN_STATE["void_reason"],
                   "anchor": dict(ANCHOR_CONTEXT)}, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)


def reset_run_state(out_dir):
    """Start a stage with a valid run and no anchor call yet.

    A stage never inherits an earlier run's void. The stage that owns the gate
    recomputes it, and every record it writes afterwards carries the fresh call.
    """
    RUN_STATE["run_valid"] = True
    RUN_STATE["void_reason"] = None
    ANCHOR_CONTEXT.update({"decision": "NOT_YET_COMPUTED", "statistic": None,
                           "band_low": None, "band_high": None, "band_half_width": None,
                           "band_centre": ANCHOR_CENTRE})
    save_run_state(out_dir)


def write_record(prov, out_dir, cell, *, values, **kwargs):
    """Write one self-describing record, with this run's validity stamped into it.

    Every record carries run_valid. Every record also carries the anchor gate's call
    and its measured band inside its own values, which the design asks for by name,
    so no reader has to fetch a separate roll-up to learn that a number is void.
    """
    v = dict(values)
    v["run_valid"] = bool(RUN_STATE["run_valid"])
    v["run_void_reason"] = RUN_STATE["void_reason"]
    v["anchor_gate_decision"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["decision"]
    v["anchor_statistic"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["statistic"]
    v["anchor_band_low"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["band_low"]
    v["anchor_band_high"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["band_high"]
    v["anchor_band_half_width"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["band_half_width"]
    v["anchor_band_centre"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["band_centre"]
    path = Path(out_dir) / (prov.cell_slug(cell) + ".json")
    prov.write_result(path, cell=cell, values=v, **kwargs)
    print("[record] %s valid=%s -> %s"
          % (kwargs.get("decision", ""), RUN_STATE["run_valid"], path.name))

def void_the_run(reason: str, out_dir):
    """Mark this run void. Every record written after this carries the flag."""
    RUN_STATE["run_valid"] = False
    RUN_STATE["void_reason"] = reason
    save_run_state(out_dir)
    print("[void] %s" % reason)


def save_run_state(out_dir):
    with open(Path(out_dir) / "run_state.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump({"run_valid": RUN_STATE["run_valid"],
                   "void_reason": RUN_STATE["void_reason"],
                   "anchor": dict(ANCHOR_CONTEXT)}, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)


def reset_run_state(out_dir):
    """Start a stage with a valid run and no anchor call yet.

    A stage never inherits an earlier run's void. The stage that owns the gate
    recomputes it, and every record it writes afterwards carries the fresh call.
    """
    RUN_STATE["run_valid"] = True
    RUN_STATE["void_reason"] = None
    ANCHOR_CONTEXT.update({"decision": "NOT_YET_COMPUTED", "statistic": None,
                           "band_low": None, "band_high": None, "band_half_width": None,
                           "band_centre": ANCHOR_CENTRE})
    save_run_state(out_dir)


def write_record(prov, out_dir, cell, *, values, **kwargs):
    """Write one self-describing record, with this run's validity stamped into it.

    Every record carries run_valid. Every record also carries the anchor gate's call
    and its measured band inside its own values, which the design asks for by name,
    so no reader has to fetch a separate roll-up to learn that a number is void.
    """
    v = dict(values)
    v["run_valid"] = bool(RUN_STATE["run_valid"])
    v["run_void_reason"] = RUN_STATE["void_reason"]
    v["anchor_gate_decision"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["decision"]
    v["anchor_statistic"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["statistic"]
    v["anchor_band_low"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["band_low"]
    v["anchor_band_high"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["band_high"]
    v["anchor_band_half_width"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["band_half_width"]
    v["anchor_band_centre"] = ANCHOR_CONTEXT["band_centre"]
    path = Path(out_dir) / (prov.cell_slug(cell) + ".json")
    prov.write_result(path, cell=cell, values=v, **kwargs)
    print("[record] %s valid=%s -> %s"
          % (kwargs.get("decision", ""), RUN_STATE["run_valid"], path.name))
    sys.stdout.flush()
    return path

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# On-box runner for the character-count repeating-pattern measurement in experiment
     3	# directory manifold_c. One public checkpoint of one open language model, one
     4	# committed text file, no text generation anywhere.
     5	#
     6	# WHAT IT RUNS, in the order the committed gate commit pins:
     7	#   1. self-tests, on the processor, before any graphics-card time;
     8	#   2. extract    one forward pass per text variant, 48 documents at nine wrap widths;
     9	#   3. calibrate  every remaining constant, from training documents alone, committed
    10	#                 to disk before any held-out number exists;
    11	#   4. endpoints  the only step that reads held-out documents.
    12	# The three steps are dependent, not parallel legs: step 3 reads what step 2 saved and
    13	# step 4 refuses to start without step 3's committed record. A failed step marks every
    14	# step that depends on it as skipped, records every exit code, and exits non-zero.
    15	#
    16	# WHY THERE IS NO VIRTUAL ENVIRONMENT HERE, and no torch install. The build template
    17	# asks for both. The bootstrap script this runner starts inside, remote_run.sh, is
    18	# frozen, refuses to build one, and says why at length: this machine image ships a
    19	# working graphics-card build of torch, no pinned replacement resolves against its

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 8. Stage one: check the inputs, run the forward passes, save the running sums.
#
# 48 documents at nine wrap widths is 432 forward passes. Nothing here reads a
# held-out number: it only writes down what the two later stages consume. The ridge
# fits are accumulated as running sums, so no stage ever holds all the hidden states.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

GROUP_NAMES = (["train_fold%d" % f for f in range(N_FOLDS)]
               + ["train_w%d" % ANCHOR_WIDTH]
               + ["test_w%d" % w for w in WIDTHS])


def group_index(name):
    return GROUP_NAMES.index(name)


def fold_of_documents(train_ids):
    """Which of the five cross-validation groups each training document belongs to.

    Splitting by document, not by position, keeps one document's sentences out of
    both sides of a split. The seed is derived from the one base seed and recorded.
    """
    import numpy as np
    seed = derived_seed("fold_split")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    order = list(rng.permutation(len(train_ids)))
    assign = {}
    for rank, pos in enumerate(order):
        assign[int(train_ids[int(pos)])] = rank % N_FOLDS
    return assign, seed


def model_kwargs(token):
    kw = {"revision": REVISION}
    if token:
        kw["token"] = token
    return kw


def load_model_in_float16(model_id, kw):
    """Load the model in float16, tolerating either spelling of the dtype argument."""
    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
    try:
        return AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.float16, **kw)
    except TypeError:
        return AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, torch_dtype=torch.float16, **kw)

Box launched. Status so far:

**Done**
- Read frozen parts: `pipeline.js` (v2.2, three modes), `triage_workflow.js`, gates, `frozen/` launcher + bootstrap + provenance writer. None edited.
- **design mode** ran: 10 arms, 7 endpoints, budget $4 (cap 15). Diff phase raised 5 departure questions. Triage grounding came back **diverges** — the reader found that the anchor band's centre (0.781) belongs to a *pooled-over-widths* fit, while the anchor statistic is *width-140-only*; this project's own committed width-140 numbers are 0.700601 / 0.664024 / 0.549. It predicts the run voids.
- Wrote `out/GATE_COMMIT_seedC1.md`: 15 items answered of record (5 diff questions, 1 grounding divergence, 1 run-queue, 1 author-queue, 7 instrument validations). Band centre **not moved** — moving a pre-registered band because a prediction says it will fail is the failure this harness exists to stop. Instead: five sibling fit readings recorded, never gated, so a void can be told apart from a construct mismatch.
- **build mode** ran: GateCheck 15/15 answered, 0 unanswered. Built `run_seedC1.py` (3102 lines) + `onbox_seedC1.sh`. Selftest: 189 checks, PASS locally, including the planted gate-failure void propagation and the planted zero-dispersion `WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE` halt.
- Reviewed both files myself: anchor fit at width 140 alone, main probe pooled over nine widths, stage order extract → calibrate → endpoints with the band committed before any test row, void stamped into every record.
- Per-launch launcher copy `out/lambda_run_seedC1_launch1.sh` — diff vs frozen is header + payload block only, every billing-safety mechanism byte-identical.

**Running**
- `gpu_1x_a100_sxm4` @ us-west-2, $1.99/hr, instance `71a83ac35d244fe1bc5a51053629dee5`, booting. Expected 15–25 min on box, ~$1.

Teardown will be confirmed via the API either way.

    doc_vec = np.zeros((N_TRAIN_DOCS, n_read, dim), dtype=np.float64)
    doc_cross = np.zeros((N_TRAIN_DOCS, n_read, dim), dtype=np.float64)
    doc_label_sum = np.zeros(N_TRAIN_DOCS, dtype=np.float64)
    doc_label_sq = np.zeros(N_TRAIN_DOCS, dtype=np.float64)
    doc_n = np.zeros(N_TRAIN_DOCS, dtype=np.int64)
    doc_order = sorted(train_ids)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 6. Ridge fitting from running sums.
#
# Holding every internal vector of every position would need many gigabytes and is
# not needed. A ridge fit and its fit quality depend on the data only through five
# running sums per layer: the sum of outer products of the vectors, the sum of the
# vectors, the sum of vector times label, the sum of labels, and the sum of squared
# labels. The extract stage accumulates those, so the later stages never hold the
# hidden states at all.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def centred_system(gram, vec_sum, cross, label_sum, n):
    """The fit's normal equations with the mean removed. Needs numpy.

    Built once per fit set and reused across ridge strengths, so the whole grid costs
    one system rather than eight.
    """
    import numpy as np
    xbar = vec_sum / n
    ybar = label_sum / n
    return gram - np.outer(vec_sum, vec_sum) / n, cross - vec_sum * ybar, xbar, ybar


def solve_ridge(centred_gram, centred_cross, xbar, ybar, alpha):
    """Weights and offset at one ridge strength. Needs numpy."""
    import numpy as np
    a = centred_gram.copy()
    dim = a.shape[0]
    a.flat[::dim + 1] += alpha            # the same as adding alpha times the identity
    weights = np.linalg.solve(a, centred_cross)
    return weights, ybar - float(weights @ xbar)


def ridge_fit_from_sums(gram, vec_sum, cross, label_sum, n, alpha):
    """Weights and offset of a ridge fit, from running sums. Needs numpy."""
    gc, cc, xbar, ybar = centred_system(gram, vec_sum, cross, label_sum, n)
    return solve_ridge(gc, cc, xbar, ybar, alpha)


def r2_from_sums(weights, offset, gram, vec_sum, cross, label_sum, label_sq_sum, n):
    """Fit quality on a group of positions, from that group's running sums. Needs numpy."""
    sse = (float(weights @ gram @ weights)
           + 2.0 * offset * float(weights @ vec_sum)
           - 2.0 * float(weights @ cross)
           + n * offset * offset
           - 2.0 * offset * label_sum
           + label_sq_sum)
    sstot = label_sq_sum - (label_sum * label_sum) / n
    if sstot <= 0:
        raise Halt("the held-out labels have no spread, so fit quality is undefined")
    return 1.0 - sse / sstot, sse, sstot


def strength_is_interior(alpha, grid) -> bool:
    """True when the winning ridge strength is not at either end of the grid."""
    ordered = sorted(grid)
    return not (alpha == ordered[0] or alpha == ordered[-1])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def pair_index_lists(label_values, profile_length: int):
    """For each distance, the row pairs of the similarity structure that distance averages.

    `label_values` are the labels that actually have an average vector, in ascending
    order, and the row of the similarity structure is the position in that list. A
    label the held-out documents never carry has no average vector and so enters no
    pair; the distance it would have contributed to simply averages fewer pairs, and
    the count is recorded. Returns one (rows, columns) pair of lists per distance.
    """
    pos = {int(v): i for i, v in enumerate(label_values)}
    out = []
    for d in range(1, profile_length + 1):
        rows = []
        cols = []
        for v in label_values:
            w = int(v) + d
            j = pos.get(w)
            if j is not None:
                rows.append(pos[int(v)])
                cols.append(j)
        out.append((rows, cols))
    return out

    """The profile and its pair counts, from a similarity structure. Pure Python."""
    pairs = pair_index_lists(label_values, profile_length)
    profile = []
    counts = []
    for d, (rows, cols) in enumerate(pairs, start=1):
        counts.append(len(rows))
        if not rows:
            raise Halt("distance %d averages zero label pairs, so the profile is undefined "
                       "there; the committed profile length may not be shortened after the "
                       "fact" % d)
        total = 0.0
        for i, j in zip(rows, cols):
            total += matrix[i][j]
        profile.append(total / len(rows))
    return profile, counts

def _trig_table(n: int, cycles):
    key = (n, tuple(cycles))
    tab = _TRIG_CACHE.get(key)
    if tab is None:
        tab = []
        for k in cycles:
            row = []
            for t in range(n):
                ang = 2.0 * math.pi * k * t / n
                row.append((math.cos(ang), math.sin(ang)))
            tab.append(row)
        _TRIG_CACHE[key] = tab
    return tab


def whole_cycle_periods(profile_length: int, period_min: float = PERIOD_MIN):
    """Every whole number of cycles across the profile, with its period in characters.

    The period of k cycles is the profile length divided by k. The design searches
    every period from 4 characters up to the profile's own length, so k runs from 1
    upward while the period stays at or above 4. Longest period first.
    """
    out = []
    k = 1
    while True:
        period = profile_length / float(k)
        if period < period_min - 1e-9:

        if period <= profile_length + 1e-9:

    n = len(y)
    tab = _trig_table(n, cycles)
    out = []
    for row in tab:
        re = 0.0
        im = 0.0
        for t in range(n):
            c, s = row[t]
            re += y[t] * c
            im -= y[t] * s
        out.append((re * re + im * im) / (n * n))

    """The statistic: the largest power over every searched period.

    Ties are broken toward the longer period, so the answer never depends on the
    order the periods are visited in.
    """
    detrended = poly_detrend(profile, degree)
    cycles = [k for k, _ in periods]
    powers = dft_power(detrended, cycles)
    best = 0
    for i in range(1, len(powers)):

    return {
        "max_power": powers[best],
        "wavelength": periods[best][1],
        "cycles": periods[best][0],
        "n_periods": len(periods),
        "powers": powers,
        "detrended": detrended,
    }

# Deviations, seed C1

Every departure from the pipeline's own procedure, booked as it happened. None of
these changes a threshold, a band, a decision rule, or any measured number.

## D1. Launch 1 failed on a defect in the built runner; the operating session fixed two lines rather than re-running the build stage

**When.** 2026-08-26, first launch. Instance `71a83ac35d244fe1bc5a51053629dee5`,
`gpu_1x_a100_sxm4`, us-west-2. The box ran about 16 minutes, of which the
measurement ran 60 seconds before failing.

**What failed.** The extract step completed all 432 forward passes and then died
writing its own output:

```
  File "/home/ubuntu/mats_manifold/run_seedC1.py", line 1389, in stage_extract
    np.savez(work_dir / "doc_sums_w%d.npz" % ANCHOR_WIDTH,
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for %: 'PosixPath' and 'int'
```

In Python `/` binds tighter than `%`, so the expression built a path and then
tried to format the path, instead of formatting the name and then joining it.
The same defect sat two lines later, at the companion save for the three probe
windows. Every read-back site in the same file already used the parenthesised
form, so the two write sites were the only ones wrong.

**Why the self-test did not catch it.** The build brief requires the self-test to
be standard-library only, so that a broken instrument shows on the processor
before any graphics-card time is spent. That requirement is what made the
self-test skip these two lines: they are the only code in the extract step that
calls into the array library to write a file, and a standard-library-only test
cannot reach them. The self-test's 189 checks all passed, on this workstation and
again on the box, and were right to.

**What was changed.** Exactly two characters classes, on lines 1389 and 1394 of
`run_seedC1.py`:

```
-    np.savez(work_dir / "doc_sums_w%d.npz" % ANCHOR_WIDTH,
+    np.savez(work_dir / ("doc_sums_w%d.npz" % ANCHOR_WIDTH),
-        np.savez(work_dir / "act_meta_a%d.npz" % a,
+        np.savez(work_dir / ("act_meta_a%d.npz" % a),
```

Nothing else in the file was touched. The self-test was re-run and still passes,
exit 0. A scan for the same precedence pattern across the whole file returns
nothing further.

**Why this was a fix and not a halt.** The pipeline's law is that no agent repairs
INFRASTRUCTURE: anything in `frozen/` that is not runnable as given must halt and
be reported, never patched. `run_seedC1.py` is not infrastructure. It is this
run's own build-stage output, and repairing a defect in it is the operating
session's job. No frozen file was touched: `pipeline.js`, `triage_workflow.js`,
`gates/` and `frozen/` are byte-identical to how they were found. No threshold,
band, bin edge, seed, or decision rule was touched. The committed design record
and gate commit are unchanged, and their hashes, which the runner carries as
constants and stamps into every record, still match.

**Cost.** About 16 minutes of one box at 1.99 USD per hour, roughly 0.53 USD,
against this seed's 15 USD cap. Teardown was confirmed through the cloud API: the
first terminate call failed on a transient network error, the launcher's retry
loop succeeded on the second try, and the instance moved to `terminating` and
then out of the account's instance list.

**What was kept.** The failed launch's artifacts are kept under
`out/results_seedC1_launch1_failed/`, including the extract step's own log, both
self-test logs, the setup-check record, and the per-position and per-variant row
files it did manage to write. They are evidence about the instrument, not about
the model, and no number in them enters any endpoint.

## D2. The build stage's template named a stage this design cannot have, and a package step the frozen bootstrap forbids

**What.** The build brief asks for stages named extract / generate / endpoints and
for the on-box script to create a virtual environment and install packages. This
design generates no text at all, and `frozen/remote_run.sh` explicitly refuses a
virtual environment and does the installs itself, with a recorded past incident
behind each refusal.

**Resolution.** The build agent followed the two binding files, which is what the
execution directive told it to do: stages are extract / calibrate / endpoints,
`--stage generate` exits 2 with an explanation, and the on-box script only
verifies what the frozen bootstrap left behind. Booked here because it is a
visible departure from the pipeline's own template wording.

content.content:
Q1 Why does the detected repeating pattern always land at exactly half the tested width, for every width and for both ways of counting position, with no exception?
   where: In the three character-based pattern files (widths 140, 200, 280) and the two working sub-word-count control files (widths 200, 280), the field recording how many full waves fit the tested width is 2 in every single case. Widths 140, 200, and 280 give wavelengths of 70, 100, and 140 characters; the sub-word versions give 100 and 140 characters again after conversion.
   if_true: If a method always reports two full waves no matter the width or how position is counted, that outcome may come from the method itself. It could come from how the curve is straightened before searching, or from the few example pairs available at the largest gaps between positions.
   changes: This would mean the headline finding, that the wave's length grows with the tested width, may be produced by the measuring method rather than by anything in the network. No later width, however chosen, could then be trusted to tell a real wave from this same artifact.

Q2 Why did the gatekeeping check land far above its allowed range, when three past readings of the same kind of check (0.700601, 0.549000, 0.664024) all sat far below it?
   where: The gatekeeping check scored 0.859740, against an allowed range of 0.767394 to 0.794606. This sits in the file recording that check and in a second file listing past readings side by side with this one. The document written before the run predicted failure from the low side, citing those same past readings.
   if_true: If the check fails high while every warning beforehand pointed to failing low, the reasoning used to anticipate trouble was wrong about which direction trouble would come from.
   changes: This would mean the project does not yet understand why this checkpoint behaves as it does on this check. Any explanation offered for the failure needs to account for the wrong-direction miss, not just the miss itself.

Q3 Why did five separate re-checks, meant to measure how much this check naturally varies, all pick the exact same brain layer and the exact same regularization strength?
   where: The calibration file lists five re-checks, one per row; all five picked layer 7 and strength 100.0. The same file flags the resulting allowed range as unusually narrow, below a limit the project had set for itself in advance.
   if_true: If five independent re-checks show zero disagreement on which layer or strength to use, the range built from them is far tighter than ordinary variation between different sets of documents would produce.
   changes: This would mean the gatekeeping check could reject a run for reasons having nothing to do with the model being studied. The project's own written concern, that too narrow a range could do exactly this, would be confirmed rather than ruled out.

Q4 Where are the line-by-line measurements for the six text-wrapping widths that fed into the single most consequential choice of this run, which brain layer to study?
   where: The file choosing which layer to study draws on documents wrapped at nine different widths. The per-line raw file provided alongside it only contains lines for three of those nine widths; the other six widths' lines are not present anywhere in this run's output.
   if_true: If the raw lines behind six of the nine widths were never kept, nobody can check, line by line, whether the layer choice was computed correctly.
   changes: This would mean the layer every later test depends on rests on numbers that cannot be independently checked from what this run saved. Only the already-summed totals remain available to trust or question.

Q5 Why does the number of directions needed to capture this signal now come out around 93 to 196, when a closely related earlier run on the same question found just 1?
   where: The three pattern-detection files each record how many directions out of 1024 are needed to capture 95 percent of the signal's spread: 93, 141, and 196 for the three widths. A separate document describes the earlier related run finding this number to be 1, with a single direction carrying 95.3 percent.
   if_true: If the same kind of signal now needs roughly a hundred to two hundred directions instead of one, its basic shape has changed enormously between the two runs.
   changes: This would call into question whether the theory that motivated this whole redesign, built on a signal packed into one direction, still describes what is being measured now.

Q6 Why is this signal detectable for line lengths from 211 to 280 characters, not detectable for 176 to 210, yet nothing explains the gap between those two ranges?
   where: The file checking whether long line lengths are measurable at all lists eight ranges of line length; it marks the fourth-from-last range as not detected while marking the two ranges beyond it as detected.
   if_true: If detectability skips one range and then returns in a farther range, a simple story of the signal fading out with distance from the training documents does not fit.
   changes: This would weaken the reasoning used elsewhere in the design: that a missing signal at long line lengths simply means it was never measurable there. Here it is measurable, then not, then measurable again.

Q7 Does picking the one brain layer to study by testing which layer fits best on the same 12 documents used afterward for the pattern check give that layer a hidden advantage?
   where: The design instructs that the layer be chosen by scoring fit directly on the 12 held-out documents; the resulting choice, layer 5, is then reused to run every later pattern check on those identical 12 documents.
   if_true: If the very same 12 documents both choose the layer and then judge whether that layer shows a pattern, the layer may look better than it would on genuinely fresh documents.
   changes: This would mean the pattern check's apparent strength cannot be treated as fully independent evidence, since the documents that picked the layer are the same ones grading it afterward.

Q8 Why does one line-length overflow at width 140 get explicitly flagged as impossible to compute, while similar overflows at widths 200 and 280 pass with no flag at all?
   where: At width 140, the sub-word-count control file states plainly that no held-out document reaches the needed line length, so it cannot be computed. At widths 200 and 280, the same kind of file lists zero missing labels, even though the raw per-line file contains one line at width 200 and two lines at width 280 that run longer than the range fixed from training documents alone.

   changes: This would mean that field cannot be trusted as a complete list of data problems for this run or for any future run with a larger overrun of the same kind.

content.content:
# Does a line-wrap wave reflect the model, or the ruler used to measure it?

This file explains one completed measurement run, in plain language. It is
written for a reader who has never seen this project before.

One model and one snapshot were studied throughout. It is a small, openly
available language model named Pythia-410m-deduped. It was tested at one
frozen training snapshot named step143000, with no changes made to it.
Below, this is called the base checkpoint.

## The question this run was testing

Some language models build an internal number line while reading wrapped
text. It is a running count of characters since the start of the current
line. A 2025 study of a much larger, closed model found that this number
line was not a smooth ramp. It carried a faint, repeating wave on top of the
ramp, like ripples over a straight line. That study explained the wave as a
side effect of squeezing a shape into too little room. The shape would
naturally need about 150 independent directions. Only about 6 were actually
available to it.

An earlier run in this project looked for the same kind of wave on the base
checkpoint. That run tested only one line-width setting. On the base
checkpoint, it found the wave's shape needed only 1 direction to hold 95.3
percent of it. If a wave truly needs only 1 direction, its predicted length
is just the chosen line width. Testing one width alone can never tell a real
wave from an artifact of picking that width.

This run tested three line widths at once, on the base checkpoint: 140,
200, and 280 characters per line. Where a wave beats pure chance at more
than one width, does its length in characters stay fixed? Or does it grow
together with the width instead? A fixed length would point to a real
feature of the model. A length that grows with the width would point to an
artifact of the ruler. Two other outcomes were allowed for: a mixed
pattern, or too few widths clearing chance to decide at all. If no width
showed any wave, that alone would be a strong negative finding, on the base
checkpoint. The one exception: a separate check might show the model was
never tracking position that far into a line to begin with.

## What the run measured

Forty-eight short public-domain texts were each wrapped onto lines, at nine
different widths. Thirty-six of the texts trained a simple statistical
readout. Twelve were held back purely for testing, in a fixed, prearranged
order.

A simple statistical readout was trained to predict each word's character
position within its line. It was trained separately at each of 25 evenly
spaced points inside the network, on the base checkpoint. The very first
point is the raw input embedding.

Exploratory, not itself a test of the wave: one of those 25 points was
picked. It became the single point used for every wave search below. The
pick used the best prediction accuracy, on the base checkpoint, on the 12
held-out test texts, pooled across all nine widths. That turned out to be
the sixth point, counting the input embedding as the first.

Exploratory, and separate from the choice above: a second best-point search
used only 140-character-wide texts. It picked the point used purely for one
required sanity check, described next.

For each of the three widths, at the one point chosen above, every
character position's internal pattern was compared against every other
position's pattern. This search was looking for a repeating wave. Each
search was scored against 200 random shuffles of the position labels. That
comparison shows what a wave would look like from pure chance alone.

A parallel control repeated the same wave search. It counted whole sub-word
pieces since the line began, instead of characters. This checked whether
any wave found was really about counting characters. It could instead be an
artifact of counting sub-word pieces.

A separate check asked whether positions past character 150 into a line
were represented by the network at all. It split the 280-character test
texts into eight slices of 35 positions each. Prediction accuracy inside
each slice was tested against that same slice's own scrambled-label
comparison.

Before trusting any wave result, one required sanity check had to pass
first. It measured held-out prediction accuracy at the sanity check's own
chosen point, using only 140-character-wide test texts. That number had to
fall inside an allowed range, built from a past run's committed number.
Falling outside it would mean the run is a broken measuring instrument.
Every wave result from a broken instrument counts as not being evidence
about the model at all.

## What was predicted, and what happened

The required sanity check was predicted to land inside an allowed range, on
the base checkpoint: 0.767394 to 0.794606. On that same base checkpoint,
the range was centred on 0.781, a number carried over from an earlier run
of this project.

The measured value, on the base checkpoint, came out to 0.859740. That
falls outside the allowed range, above its high end.

falls outside the allowed range, above its high end.

That is a failed sanity check. By this run's own rule, every later
measurement, on the base checkpoint, is void. None of it is evidence about
the model. It only shows the measuring setup drifted from the earlier run
it was calibrated against.

The numbers below were still computed and saved. They are worth reporting
for what they show. Every one of them carries that same void label.

All three widths beat pure chance, on the base checkpoint. The observed
wave strength ranked first out of 200 random-shuffle comparisons, at every
one of the three widths tested.

On the base checkpoint, the 140-character width gave a wave length of 70
characters. The 200-character width gave 100 characters, and the
280-character width gave 140 characters. Each is exactly half of its own
width.

The longest and shortest of those lengths differ by 70 characters. That is
more than the 10-character difference allowed for calling them one fixed
length. All three lengths sit at exactly half their own width. On that same base
checkpoint, that is a matching ratio of 0.5 in every case. So the headline
call, on the base checkpoint, is that the wave's length grows with the
width. That call is
void, for the reason above.

At the 140-character width, the sub-word-piece control could not even be
computed. No held-out test text reached the sub-word position the
comparison needed. At the 200-character width, the two ways of counting
position gave wave lengths 15.277055 characters apart, on the base
checkpoint. At the 280-character width, they gave wave lengths 17.735970
characters apart, on the base checkpoint. Both gaps pass the 3-character
cutoff for treating the two as the same wave. So the wave at those two
widths is credited to counting characters, not to counting sub-word pieces.

The escape-hatch check looked past character 150 into a line, on the base
checkpoint. Both far ends tested were represented there: positions 211
through 245, and positions 246 through 280. So the void above is not
explained away as nothing being measurable that far into a line.

## Does this match what was expected

No, on more than one count. This section says so plainly rather than
smoothing it over.

Before the run, the recorded concern was that the sanity check would most
likely fail low. Three past readings of this exact 140-character-only
measurement, on the base checkpoint, were 0.700601, 0.549000, and 0.664024.
All three, on that same base checkpoint, sat below the allowed range's low
end of 0.767394. The check instead failed high, on the base checkpoint, at
0.859740. That is the opposite direction from the one anticipated.

An earlier, closely related run, on the base checkpoint, had found this
same kind of wave needing only 1 direction. On that same base checkpoint,
that single direction carried 95.3 percent of the wave's shape. This run
instead needed 93 to 196 directions, on the same base checkpoint, across
its three widths, to reach that same 95 percent mark.
That is a large, unexplained change in the wave's basic shape between the
two runs.

Because the required sanity check failed, this run's outcome is neither of
the two rival ideas it set out to test. It is not "the wave has one fixed
length." It is not "the wave's length is an artifact of the width" either.
It is a third outcome, on the base checkpoint: the run cannot be read as
evidence for or against either idea. Every wave number above is exploratory
only, kept for the record. None of it is usable as a finding about the
model.

These are open questions raised about this run. A few more that this review
turned up on its own follow them.

**The wave's length always came out to exactly half the width tested.**
Counting by character or by sub-word piece made no difference. At every
width tried (140, 200, and 280 characters), the found wave completed
exactly 2 full cycles across the tested span, with no exception. A method
that always reports two cycles, regardless of width or counting scheme, may
be producing that number itself. It may not be detecting it in the network.

**The sanity check failed on the wrong side.** Going in, every recorded
warning pointed toward a low failure. That warning rested on three past
readings of the same measurement. The check instead failed high. Whatever
reasoning predicted trouble was reasoning about the wrong direction. That
weakens confidence in the rest of that reasoning.

**Five reruns meant to measure this run's own natural variation all landed
on the identical choice.** Five reruns, each holding out a different six
documents, were meant to show how much the sanity check's result would
normally wander. All five picked the identical internal point and the
identical readout strength. The resulting allowed range came out narrower
